notes: THE UNIT IS THE CHAPTER. The director picks nine chapter types; each one
expands to its own small shot list from templates/chapters/. Nobody
authors 270 shots.
THE ROOM IS A LOBBY. A chapter opens in the room, DIVES INTO THE MONITOR
where the substance happens, and surfaces back to close before the next
stinger. dive-in and dive-out run once or twice per chapter across nine
chapters, which makes them the most-used motion in the format.
Pacing is 4-8s per shot and the host is present far more than in a short —
NOT the 1.5-3s cutting the old long used, which is what made it read as a
collage.
PROGRESSION IS ON, and it is the only format that turns it on. Whatever
clutter state a chapter names is re-pointed by where the shot sits in the
runtime: the light goes daylight -> afternoon -> dusk -> 3am, the room
fills, the evidence wall fills, the clock reads the light's hour, and the
steam, the cursor and the second hand run underneath. None of it is
anything a chapter can ask for. See pipeline/progression.py.
FULL COVERAGE IS RESERVED FOR THE CHAPTER BOUNDARY. ink-wipe-16 runs at
the top of every chapter and nowhere else; the shorts use underline-swipe
between beats, because a black wipe every four seconds is a slideshow.
The boundary is applied by the chapter expansion, not written into nine
chapter files - a chapter type does not know it is a chapter of a long.
